def-source-target-distributions-and-shif:
## Definition

Let $(\mathsf X,\Sigma_X)$, $(\mathsf Y,\Sigma_Y)$, and $(\mathsf A,\Sigma_A)$ be nonempty measurable spaces. A **source/target pair of joint laws** consists of probability measures $P_S$ and $P_T$ on $(\mathsf X\times\mathsf Y,\Sigma_X\otimes\Sigma_Y)$. For $D\in\{S,T\}$, its input marginal is the probability measure $\mu_D$ on $(\mathsf X,\Sigma_X)$ defined by $\mu_D(A)=P_D(A\times\mathsf Y)$. If $h:\mathsf X\to\mathsf A$ is measurable and $\ell:\mathsf A\times\mathsf Y\to[0,+\infty]$ is product-measurable, then $(x,y)\mapsto(h(x),y)$ is measurable: the preimage of a measurable rectangle $U\times V$ is $h^{-1}(U)\times V$, and such rectangles generate the product sigma-algebra. Taking preimages once more shows that $(x,y)\mapsto\ell(h(x),y)$ is measurable. The domain risk is the extended nonnegative integral
$$R_D(h):=\int_{\mathsf X\times\mathsf Y}\ell(h(x),y)\,P_D(d(x,y)).$$

A **conditional label kernel** for $P_D$ is a specified probability kernel $K_D$ from $(\mathsf X,\Sigma_X)$ to $(\mathsf Y,\Sigma_Y)$ such that, for every nonnegative product-measurable $g:\mathsf X\times\mathsf Y\to[0,+\infty]$,
$$\int g(x,y)\,P_D(d(x,y))=\int_{\mathsf X}\left(\int_{\mathsf Y}g(x,y)\,K_D(x,dy)\right)\mu_D(dx).$$
The pair is under **covariate shift** when conditional label kernels $K_S,K_T$ are supplied, there is a measurable set $N$ with $\mu_T(N)=0$ such that $K_S(x,\cdot)=K_T(x,\cdot)$ as probability measures for every $x\notin N$, and $\mu_T\ll\mu_S$. No existence of conditional kernels is asserted by this definition.
def-h-delta-h-divergence:
## Definition

Let $(\mathsf X,\Sigma_X)$ be a measurable space, equip $\{0,1\}$ with its discrete sigma-algebra, let $\mu_S$ and $\mu_T$ be probability measures on $\mathsf X$, and let $\mathcal H$ be a nonempty class of measurable classifiers $h:\mathsf X\to\{0,1\}$. For $h,h'\in\mathcal H$, define their measurable disagreement set by
$$A_{h,h'}:=\bigl(h^{-1}(\{0\})\cap h'^{-1}(\{1\})\bigr)\cup\bigl(h^{-1}(\{1\})\cap h'^{-1}(\{0\})\bigr).$$
The **$\mathcal H\Delta\mathcal H$ divergence** of the two input laws is
$$d_{\mathcal H\Delta\mathcal H}(\mu_S,\mu_T):=2\sup_{h,h'\in\mathcal H}\left|\mu_S(A_{h,h'})-\mu_T(A_{h,h'})\right|\in[0,2].$$
def-loss-discrepancy-between-domains:
## Definition

Let $(\mathsf X,\Sigma_X)$ and $(\mathsf Y,\Sigma_Y)$ be measurable spaces, let $P$ and $Q$ be probability measures on $\mathsf X$ (in particular, source and target input marginals), and let $\mathcal H$ be a nonempty class of measurable functions $h:\mathsf X\to\mathsf Y$. Let $L:\mathsf Y\times\mathsf Y\to[0,+\infty]$ be product-measurable. For $h,h'\in\mathcal H$, the map $x\mapsto(h'(x),h(x))$ is measurable because the preimage of each measurable rectangle $A\times B$ is $h'^{-1}(A)\cap h^{-1}(B)$ and such rectangles generate the product sigma-algebra; composing with $L$ shows that $x\mapsto L(h'(x),h(x))$ is measurable. Assume that, for every $h,h'\in\mathcal H$, the two integrals below are finite, and define
$$L_P(h',h):=\int_{\mathsf X}L(h'(x),h(x))\,P(dx),\qquad L_Q(h',h):=\int_{\mathsf X}L(h'(x),h(x))\,Q(dx).$$
The **$L$-discrepancy** between $P$ and $Q$ over $\mathcal H$ is the extended nonnegative number
$$\operatorname{disc}_L(P,Q):=\sup_{h,h'\in\mathcal H}\left|L_P(h',h)-L_Q(h',h)\right|\in[0,+\infty].$$
The supremum need not be attained.
lem-covariate-shift-joint-law-density:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $P_S,P_T$ be source and target joint laws with input marginals $\mu_S,\mu_T$ and specified conditional label kernels $K_S,K_T$ as in the definition of source/target distributions. Suppose $\mu_T\ll\mu_S$ and there is a $\mu_T$-null set outside of which $K_S(x,\cdot)=K_T(x,\cdot)$. Let $w$ be any nonnegative measurable representative of $d\mu_T/d\mu_S$. Then for every product-measurable set $E\subseteq\mathsf X\times\mathsf Y$,
$$P_T(E)=\int_E w(x)\,P_S(d(x,y)).$$
Consequently $P_T\ll P_S$ and $w\circ\pi_X$ is a representative of the likelihood-ratio density of $P_T$ with respect to $P_S$.
thm-covariate-shift-importance-weighting:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $P_S,P_T$ be source and target joint laws under covariate shift, with input marginals $\mu_S,\mu_T$ and common conditional label kernel $K$. Let $w$ be a nonnegative measurable representative of $d\mu_T/d\mu_S$. For any measurable predictor $h$ and nonnegative product-measurable loss $\ell$, if the weighted source loss is integrable, then
$$R_T(h)=\int_{\mathsf X\times\mathsf Y}\ell(h(x),y)\,P_T(d(x,y))=\int_{\mathsf X\times\mathsf Y}w(x)\ell(h(x),y)\,P_S(d(x,y))<+\infty.$$
thm-target-risk-bound-by-source-risk-div:
## Statement

Let $(\mathsf X,\Sigma_X)$ be a measurable space, equip $\{0,1\}$ with its discrete sigma-algebra, and let $P_S,P_T$ be joint probability laws on $\mathsf X\times\{0,1\}$ with input marginals $\mu_S,\mu_T$. Let $\mathcal H$ be a nonempty class of measurable classifiers $h:\mathsf X\to\{0,1\}$. Define the source and target risks by $\epsilon_D(h):=P_D\{(x,y):h(x)\ne y\}$ for $D\in\{S,T\}$ and define the joint-labeling error $\lambda:=\inf_{g\in\mathcal H}(\epsilon_S(g)+\epsilon_T(g))$. Then every $h\in\mathcal H$ satisfies
$$\epsilon_T(h)\le\epsilon_S(h)+\tfrac12 d_{\mathcal H\Delta\mathcal H}(\mu_S,\mu_T)+\lambda.$$
thm-discrepancy-domain-adaptation-bound:
## Statement

Let $P,Q$ be the source and target input marginals on a common measurable space $\mathsf X$. Let $\mathsf Y$ be a measurable output space, $\mathcal H$ a nonempty class of measurable functions $h:\mathsf X\to\mathsf Y$, and $f_P,f_Q:\mathsf X\to\mathsf Y$ measurable labeling functions. Let $L:\mathsf Y\times\mathsf Y\to[0,+\infty]$ be product-measurable, symmetric, and satisfy the triangle inequality. Define
$$L_D(g_1,g_2):=\int_{\mathsf X}L(g_1(x),g_2(x))\,D(dx)\quad(D\in\{P,Q\}),\qquad \operatorname{disc}_L(P,Q):=\sup_{g_1,g_2\in\mathcal H}|L_P(g_1,g_2)-L_Q(g_1,g_2)|.$$
Assume that every pairwise integral in this discrepancy definition is finite and that source and target minimizers $h_P^*\in\arg\min_{g\in\mathcal H}L_P(g,f_P)$ and $h_Q^*\in\arg\min_{g\in\mathcal H}L_Q(g,f_Q)$ exist. Then every $h\in\mathcal H$ satisfies
$$L_P(h,f_P)\le L_P(h_P^*,f_P)+L_Q(h,h_Q^*)+\operatorname{disc}_L(P,Q)+\min\{L_Q(h_Q^*,h_P^*),L_P(h_Q^*,h_P^*)\}.$$
The supremum defining $\operatorname{disc}_L$ may be infinite, in which case the inequality is interpreted in the extended nonnegative reals.
